2664/full/standalone.answer: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining. The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance. India raised diversion risks, sought proactive involvement of the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting, and judged those concerns not fully addressed. At adoption the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime's exemption applied for two years, with the Council intending to decide on an extension.

2739/full/standalone.answer: Algeria, China and Russia abstained. The Council adopted Japanese–US draft S/2024/500 as resolution 2739 (2024), 12–0–3. The adopted text conferred no new authorization of military action. Algeria valued monthly reporting on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels to keep the Council informed. It abstained over implementation of resolution 2722 and alleged misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign territory. It extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) through 15 January 2025.
